title: Spicy Beans with Tortilla Chips
description: Spicy Beans with Tortilla Chips is a hearty Mexican appetizer featuring creamy, smoky black beans served with crispy homemade tortilla chips and topped with queso fresco, avocado, cilantro, and sour cream. Perfect for sharing as a snack or starter.

ingredients.title: For the Beans
items: Cooked black beans (or 1 can, drained & rinsed) – 2 cups
Small jalapeño, finely chopped (remove seeds for milder heat) – 1
Chipotle chili powder – ¼ tsp (optional, for smoky heat)
Vegetable or chicken stock – ½ cup
Salt & freshly ground black pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: For the Toppings
items: Crumbled queso fresco or Cotija cheese – ½ cup
Sour cream or Mexican crema – ¼ cup

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Tortilla Chips (homemade for best texture)
steps: Toss tortilla triangles with oil and a pinch of salt.
Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and golden.
Tip: For extra flavor, sprinkle with smoked paprika or chili powder before baking.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Cook the Spicy Beans
steps: Heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and jalapeño until soft and fragrant (3–4 minutes).
Stir in tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, and chipotle powder; cook 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Add the beans and stock; simmer for 5–7 minutes until thickened.
Mash slightly with a potato masher or the back of a spoon for a creamy, rustic texture.
Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice to taste.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Assemble the Dish
steps: Spread the warm spicy beans on a serving platter or individual bowls.
Arrange tortilla chips around or on top of the beans.
Garnish with queso fresco, diced avocado, cilantro, red onion, and a drizzle of sour cream.
Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve warm with freshly baked tortilla chips.
Pair with guacamole, salsa roja, or pico de gallo.
Enjoy as a shared appetizer or a light meal.

chefTips: Beans: Use freshly cooked beans for deeper flavor; canned is fine but rinse well to reduce excess salt.
Texture: Slightly mashing the beans keeps a rustic, creamy texture. Over-mashing makes it paste-like.
Spice Balance: Adjust jalapeño and chipotle powder to your desired heat level; add a pinch of sugar if beans taste too acidic.
Presentation: Serve in a shallow bowl with chips arranged around the edges and toppings artfully scattered.
